title: AI matched some team performance while changing expertise sharing and social connection in product innovation work
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33641, The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise
geography: Procter & Gamble, a US-headquartered global consumer packaged goods company; participant geography is not fully specified in the abstract

performance.value: individuals using AI matched the performance of teams working without AI
performance.unit: reported performance comparison on real product-innovation challenges

assignment.value: professionals were randomly assigned to AI or no-AI work and to individual or two-person new-product-development work

collaboration_substitute.value: AI reproduced some benefits of human collaboration on the measured tasks

observations.method: Pre-registered randomized field experiment using real product-innovation challenges, comparing AI access, no AI, individual work, and human-team work.
observations.uncertainty: Performance equivalence is task-specific and does not show that AI replaces all team functions, improves long-run innovation, or preserves worker learning, trust, or accountability.
observations.subgroup: Professionals working individually or in new-product-development teams at a global consumer packaged goods company.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI may complement teams by freeing people for other interaction rather than substitute for collaboration; the abstract does not measure completed products, market success, pay, or worker control.

observations.period: Field experiment; R&D and Commercial professional backgrounds

denominator.unit: experiment participants assessed on product-innovation proposals

without_ai_specialization.value: R&D professionals tended toward more technical proposals, while Commercial professionals leaned toward commercially oriented proposals

with_ai_balance.value: AI users produced more balanced solutions regardless of professional background

silo_effect.value: AI reduced the measured expression of functional silos in proposed solutions

observations.method: Randomized comparison of proposal content across R&D and Commercial participants with and without AI access.
observations.uncertainty: Balanced proposals are not proof of better technical validity, commercial success, equal voice, or genuine expertise integration; the study does not establish whether organizational authority changes.
observations.subgroup: R&D and Commercial professionals with different domain training and functional identities.
observations.counterinterpretation: A language interface may smooth visible differences while masking disagreement, reducing specialized depth, or shifting judgment toward the tool's defaults.

observations.period: Field experiment; self-reported emotional response during knowledge work

social_response.value: AI users reported more positive emotional responses

social_role.value: The authors suggest the language-based interface can fulfill part of the social and motivational role traditionally offered by human teammates

organizational_open_link.value: Human belonging, durable trust, worker voice, psychological safety, and team retention remain unmeasured

observations.method: Randomized field comparison with self-reported emotional responses collected during product-innovation work.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported positivity is not equivalent to durable social connection, wellbeing, trust, or team cohesion; the abstract does not provide the scale, effect size, or response timing.
observations.subgroup: Knowledge workers using AI individually or alongside human teammates in a consumer-goods innovation setting.
observations.counterinterpretation: A pleasant interface may reduce immediate friction while weakening human contact or making dissent less visible; positive affect does not establish a better workplace or consumer product.

boundary: This record adds a US-company consumer-goods workplace experiment linking AI access to performance, teamwork, expertise sharing, functional silos, and self-reported emotional response. It does not establish replacement of teams, durable expertise, worker control, pay, employment, product-market success, consumer welfare, or long-run social connection.
